newsitem.title: UK: Wash hands to stop E coli spread, experts advise.
newsitem.headline: Wash hands to stop E coli spread, experts advise.

text.p: Something as simple as regular hand washing could help reduce the spread of the E coli bacteria during food poisoning outbreaks, U.S. experts said on Friday.

Such measures would be particularly important in children's day care centres, David Swerdlow and Patricia Griffin of the Centres for Disease Control said in a commentary in the Lancet medical journal.

They were reviewing various studies on transmission of E coli 0157, a mutated version of a common gut bacteria that can cause diarrhoea and, in vulnerable young children and the elderly, fatal kidney failure and brain damage.

E coli has been blamed for 19 deaths in Scotland and 11 in Japan. It can be passed from infected meat -- usually the result of improper slaughtering -- or through fruits and vegetables that have been in contact with manure.
The bacteria is found in a victim's stool, even if symptoms are so mild that the victim is unaware of infection.
"Outbreaks of the illness due to person-to-person spread have occurred in schools, long-term care institutions, families and day-care facilities," Swerdlow and Griffin wrote.
Anyone who seems infected should be kept away from such centres until they are cleared or cured, they said.

"Routine hand washing before snacks and meals and after diaper (nappy) changes and toileting is the best way to prevent the spread of infection in day-care centres," they added. "Hand washing upon arrival would provide additional protection."

The British government is currently fighting off criticism that lax measures in slaughterhouses contributed to outbreaks of E coli food poisoning. Guidelines for preventing its spread include hosing down carcasses.
